hyps.why: Raising an already large learning rate pushes Adam into divergence.
At tiny learning rates the model is undertrained, so increasing the rate helps substantially.
Stepping down from an unstable learning rate restores convergence.
Small batches already give noisy gradients, so a larger step size destabilizes training.
Larger batches mean fewer updates, worsening underfitting when the learning rate is small.
Larger batches reduce gradient noise and stabilize high-learning-rate training.
When L2 regularization is already strong, increasing it further causes heavy underfitting.
Narrow networks are capacity-limited, so adding units yields the largest gains.
Deeper ReLU networks are more prone to instability and dead units at large learning rates.
Small-batch training benefits most from a smaller, more stable step size.
